 Jury hits Lincoln Towing with $2.85 million verdict, including record punitive damages
 October 30, 2026 5:04 AM 
 Tim Hecke 
 Citywide , Suburbs 
 Jermall Harvey, inset, and a video frame of the fateful tow. ( NBC5 Chicago ) 
 It’s a story likely to warm hearts across Chicago: A Cook County jury has ordered Lincoln Towing, one of the city’s most disliked companies, to pay $2.85 million to a man who said one of its employees pointed a gun at his head as he clung to the hood of a tow truck moving through Wicker Park traffic. And the award includes record-setting punitive damages.
 Jermall Harvey had permission to park in the lot of the now-shuttered CVS at 1200 North Ashland on October 12, 2022. When he learned that Lincoln Towing employees were preparing to tow his car, he ran outside to tell them he was parked legally and had a valid pass.
 Video aired by NBC 5 in 2023 showed Harvey jogging toward the tow truck, which appeared to speed toward the garage exit. State law requires towing companies to release a vehicle if its owner approaches before the tow is completed, the news outlet reported.
 Harvey stepped in front of the truck, hoping to stop the tow. When the driver allegedly accelerated, Harvey jumped onto the hood as the truck entered Wicker Park traffic. Then, according to Harvey’s lawsuit, the encounter took an even more alarming turn: The tow truck’s passenger pulled out a gun, pointed it at Harvey’s head and ordered him off the hood.
 Harvey remained on the hood for more than a minute as the truck traveled down Division Street. He eventually fell away, and Lincoln Towing left with his car.
 Harvey sued the company, and the case went to trial this month, culminating with the $2.85 million award. The jury sent a very clear message to Lincoln Towing, too: Nearly two-thirds of the award consisted of punitive damages. According to the Jury Verdict Reporter, that’s the largest reported punitive damages award in Cook County municipal districts—nearly four times the previous record, set in 1994.
